text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate logic, and give variables clearer names. This makes the code simpler to maintain and less likely to contain bugs. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Even though the program's behavior stays the same, good refactoring saves time and effort in the future. It is an essential practice for keeping software healthy and for helping teams work together more effectively.
